settings.title: Basic hand tools
settings.description: A hacksaw, files, sandpaper, a measuring tape — no power tools. Everything else is in the kit.

settings.title: A bit of space
settings.description: A sturdy table around 1200 × 600 mm and a spot the frame can sit undisturbed while joints cure.

settings.title: A few weekends
settings.description: 25–35 hours across multiple sessions. No rush — bamboo is forgiving and most mistakes are fixable.

settings.title: Set the geometry
settings.description: Set the little-rider geometry on the jig — low and stable for small legs, feet flat on the ground.

settings.title: Join & wrap
settings.description: Bond the tubes with epoxy and wrap each joint with carbon-fibre tow.

settings.title: Cure
settings.description: Leave it for a full cure — that's where maximum joint strength comes from.

settings.title: Sand, seal & ride
settings.description: Sand smooth, seal the bamboo, fit the headset and bottom bracket. Adventure awaits.

settings.question: What age and size is this for?
settings.answer: Designed for children roughly aged 2–5, as a balance (pedal-free) first bike. The right fit depends on your child's inside-leg measurement more than age — send us their height and inside leg and we'll confirm it suits them.

settings.question: Is it light enough for a toddler to handle?
settings.answer: Bamboo is naturally light and the balance frame is small, so it's made to be manageable for little legs. We don't want to publish a weight we haven't measured — please confirm the finished weight in kg before this goes live.

settings.question: Why no pedals?
settings.answer: Balance bikes teach the hard part first — balancing and steering — without pedals or stabilisers. Children glide with their feet, then move straight to a pedal bike, usually skipping stabilisers altogether.

settings.question: How hard is the build, and how long does it take?
settings.answer: It's our simplest kit — fewer parts than an adult frame and around 8–12 hours, comfortably a weekend. No power tools: just basic hand tools (hacksaw, files, sandpaper, tape) and a work surface. Most builders start with zero experience, and our community can help if you get stuck.

settings.question: Is it safe and strong enough for a child?
settings.answer: Very strong for its weight. Bamboo is a light, hollow natural composite and every joint is reinforced with carbon-fibre, giving a high strength-to-weight ratio. Our bamboo is independently tested at Swansea University. Builders ride these frames daily and tour continents — with proper care they last for years.
